## How to convert JPG to PDF online

Learn how easy it is to use our image to PDF converter to save any image as a PDF, including JPG, PNG, BMP, GIF, or TIFF files:

![https://main--dc--adobecom.aem.live/dc-shared/fragments/modals/videos/frictionless/how-to-convert-jpg-to-pdf#video \| Play video: How to convert JPG to PDF \| :play-medium][image0]

- Click the **Select a file** button above or drag and drop files into the drop zone.
- Select the image file you want to convert to PDF.
- After uploading, Acrobat automatically converts the file from an image format to PDF.
- Download your new PDF file or sign in to share it.

blocks.name: Accordion
rows: **How do I convert a JPG to PDF with Adobe Acrobat?**

To convert a JPG to PDF with Adobe Acrobat, open the online JPG to PDF tool, upload your image file, and click “Convert.” Your PDF will download in
seconds. In the Acrobat desktop app, you can also go to File > Create > PDF From File and select your JPG. Acrobat preserves the image quality and
dimensions of your original file in the resulting PDF.
**Can Adobe Acrobat combine multiple JPG images into one PDF?**

Yes, Adobe Acrobat lets you combine multiple JPG images into a single PDF by selecting all your image files and merging them in your specified order.
In the desktop app, go to File > Create > Combine Files into a Single PDF and add all your JPGs. Acrobat's online tool also allows you to upload
multiple images to convert JPGs to PDFs in batches.
**Does Adobe Acrobat support other image formats besides JPG for PDF conversion?**

Yes, Adobe Acrobat supports conversion of PNG, TIFF, BMP, and GIF image files to PDF in addition to JPG. You can mix different image formats in a
single batch conversion, and Acrobat will merge them into one unified PDF.
**Who uses Adobe Acrobat to convert JPGs to PDF?**

Business professionals archiving receipts or forms, photographers converting image portfolios, and students scanning and submitting assignment photos
commonly use Adobe Acrobat to turn JPGs into PDFs. The conversion is also popular for teams that need to send images in a non-editable, universally
viewable format. Acrobat creates PDFs that open consistently across all devices and operating systems.
**Does Adobe Acrobat reduce image quality when converting JPG to PDF?**

Adobe Acrobat preserves the original resolution of your JPG when creating a PDF unless you request to compress your file during the conversion. The
default JPG to PDF conversion in Acrobat does not degrade image quality, making it suitable for professional-quality print output. If you need smaller
file sizes, Acrobat's compression tool can optimize your PDF after it is converted.
**What is the maximum file size for JPG to PDF conversion in Adobe Acrobat?**

The Adobe Acrobat online JPG to PDF tool is compatible with files up to 100MB per upload for free conversions. Higher file size limits are available
with an Acrobat subscription. The desktop app has no practical file size restriction and is the recommended option for very large or high-resolution
image files. If you need to convert large batches of images, Adobe Acrobat Pro's batch processing tools are the most efficient option.
**Is Adobe Acrobat's JPG to PDF converter free?**

Adobe Acrobat's online JPG to PDF converter is free to use for a limited number of conversions without signing in, but you must sign in to save or
download your file. Unlimited conversions, batch uploads, and access to additional tools like merging and compression require an Acrobat subscription.
[See all plans here](https://www.adobe.com/acrobat/pricing/compare-versions.html).
